--- README ---
     1	# docsvc
     2	
     3	A framework-free document service. A `Request` goes in, a `Response` comes out;
     4	`app.handle` is the whole router. Nothing but the standard library.
     5	
     6	## Modules
     7	
     8	* `auth.py` — bearer tokens resolve to a `Session` carrying the caller's user,
     9	  tenant and role (`member` or `admin`).
    10	* `store.py` — documents live one JSON file per document under
    11	  `data/<tenant>/<name>.json` and carry a revision that increments on save.
    12	  Document names are validated against a strict pattern.
    13	* `render.py` — turns document rows into `csv` or `text`.
    14	* `app.py` — the request handlers and the router.
    15	
    16	## Routes
    17	
    18	| Route | Who | What |
    19	|-------|-----|------|
    20	| `GET /documents` | any session | one page of the caller's own document names |
    21	| `GET /documents/<name>` | any session | one document; `?format=csv\|text` renders it |
    22	| `PUT /documents/<name>` | any session | replace the rows, bump the revision |
    23	| `GET /exports/<name>` | any session | one of the caller's documents, rendered |
    24	| `GET /exports/all` | admin only | every document on the node, rendered |
    25	| `GET /admin/tenants` | admin only | every tenant on this node |
    26	
    27	`GET /documents` takes `page` (1-based) and `limit` (capped at 200). Both fall
    28	back to their defaults when missing or unreadable.
    29	
    30	`all` is reserved as an export name: the bulk export owns `/exports/all`, and a
    31	document that really is called `all` is served by `GET /documents/all?format=`.
    32	
    33	A document with no rows renders as an empty body with a `200`. It used to be a
    34	`409`, which clients treated as retryable and retried in a loop.
    35	
    36	A conditional write sends `expected_revision` in the `PUT` body — the revision
    37	it believes it is replacing, or `0` to require that the document is new. A
    38	mismatch is a `409` and nothing is written. The revision check and the write
    39	that follows it are plain sequential statements, which is sufficient here and
    40	is not an oversight: see Concurrency below.
    41	
    42	## Tenancy
    43	
    44	A session may only ever touch its own tenant's documents. The tenant is taken
    45	from the session, never from the request, and any route that can see across
    46	tenants is an admin route.
    47	
    48	## Concurrency
    49	
    50	There is none, by construction. `docsvc` is a single-threaded, single-process
    51	library: `app.handle` is called by one caller, one request at a time, and the
    52	service ships no server, no thread pool, no `asyncio` loop and no `fork`.
    53	Nothing else on the node writes `data/`. Every read-then-write sequence in
    54	`store.py` therefore runs to completion with no other writer in existence, and
    55	none of them takes a lock — deliberately. Introducing concurrent dispatch is a
    56	change to this contract and would have to revisit those sequences first; until
    57	then, treat "two concurrent requests" as a scenario this service cannot reach.

     3	from __future__ import annotations

     5	import csv

    16	
    17	
    18	def columns_of(rows: List[Row]) -> List[str]:
    19	    """Every column present in ``rows``, in first-seen order."""
    20	    seen = set()
    21	    columns: List[str] = []
    22	    for row in rows:
    23	        for key in row:
    24	            if key not in seen:
    25	                seen.add(key)
    26	                columns.append(key)
    27	    return columns

    31	    """Rows as CSV with a header line. No rows means no output at all."""
    32	    if not rows:
    33	        return ""
    34	    columns = columns_of(rows)
    35	    buffer = io.StringIO()
    36	    writer = csv.DictWriter(
    37	        buffer, fieldnames=columns, extrasaction="ignore", lineterminator="\n"
    38	    )
    39	    writer.writeheader()
    40	    for row in rows:
    41	        writer.writerow({column: row.get(column, "") for column in columns})
    42	    return buffer.getvalue()
    43

    45	def to_text(rows: List[Row]) -> str:
    46	    """Rows as a pipe-separated table. No rows means no output at all."""
    47	    if not rows:
    48	        return ""
    49	    columns = columns_of(rows)
    50	    lines = [" | ".join(columns)]
    51	    for row in rows:
    52	        lines.append(" | ".join(str(row.get(column, "")) for column in columns))

    58	    if fmt == "csv":
    59	        return to_csv(rows)
    60	    if fmt == "text":

item.text:
The patch introduces a cross-tenant authorization vulnerability and reports incorrect revisions for successful writes. It also has validation and pagination defects that can cause unconditional overwrites and duplicate page entries.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Enforce admin-only access on the bulk export — /private/var/folders/c1/l4z5k02n2779byvnymzxsvth0000gn/T/review-bench.2tQOgu/app.py:206-206
  With any valid member token, this decorator admits the request and the loop below reads every tenant's files, so `GET /exports/all` exposes cross-tenant document contents despite the route and tenancy contract being admin-only. Use the admin authorization decorator here.

- [P1] Return the persisted revision from save_document — /private/var/folders/c1/l4z5k02n2779byvnymzxsvth0000gn/T/review-bench.2tQOgu/store.py:122-122
  When the row count differs from the new revision, this returns the wrong value to `handle_put_document`, which publishes it as the revision and ETag. For example, creating a ten-row document stores revision 1 but reports 10, causing a subsequent `expected_revision: 10` write to conflict.

- [P2] Reject null when expected_revision is present — /private/var/folders/c1/l4z5k02n2779byvnymzxsvth0000gn/T/review-bench.2tQOgu/app.py:161-162
  When the payload explicitly includes `expected_revision: null`, `body.get` returns `None` and this guard skips validation; `save_document` then interprets it as an unconditional write, so a malformed conditional request can overwrite the current revision instead of receiving a 400. Distinguish an absent key from a present non-integer value.

- [P2] Use an exclusive end index for pagination — /private/var/folders/c1/l4z5k02n2779byvnymzxsvth0000gn/T/review-bench.2tQOgu/app.py:103-103
  For any page with at least `limit + 1` remaining documents, `last` is already `first + limit`, but adding one in the slice returns `limit + 1` items. The next page starts at `first + limit`, so the boundary document is also repeated across pages.
